description:
Make a new tool from the Python skeleton, or check a tool. One op per call:
- new: {"op": "new", "path": "my_tools/mul"}  (copies the skeleton: a working tool that adds two numbers; path must not exist yet; relative paths start at your workspace). Optional "description" fills in what the tool does.
- check: {"op": "check", "path": "my_tools/mul", "sample": {"a": 6, "b": 7}}  (remakes _tooldef.json and _metainfo.json from tool.py, checks them, runs the Example written in the description and tries one call with sample if given; one line per item, lines marked bad say how to fix; the last line says if it is ready)
After new: in tool.py change only the part that new prints (DESCRIPTION, PARAMS, META, run), with edit; do not rewrite the whole file (README.md there has a full example). Then check, then add it: self_tools {"op": "add", "path": "my_tools/mul"}. path for check can also be a JSON file or FILE.json#/POINTER.
Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, PathExists (pick another path), PathMissing, ToolBad (see the bad lines). Details: memory_read aos/tools.json#/tools_def.

op.description: new = copy the skeleton to a new tool folder, check = check a tool

path.description: new: the new tool folder (must not exist yet). check: the tool folder, JSON file or FILE.json#/POINTER. Relative to your workspace, or absolute

description.description: new: what the new tool does, with one example call (goes into DESCRIPTION in tool.py)

sample.description: check: arguments for one test call, like {"a": 6, "b": 7}
